title: Lemon icebox pie

items: 8 oz cream cheese, softened at room temperature about 1 hr
½ cup fresh lemon juice (from 3–4 lemons)
1 Tbsp finely grated lemon zest (from 2 lemons)
1½ cups graham cracker crumbs (about 11 full sheets)

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the middle.

Make the crust: stir the graham cracker crumbs, sugar, salt and melted butter in a bowl until it looks like wet sand. Press it firmly into the bottom and up the sides of the 9-inch glass pie plate with a flat-bottomed measuring cup.
Bake the crust 8–10 min, until fragrant and slightly darker at the edges. Cool completely on a wire rack, about 30 min. A warm crust softens the filling.
Beat the cream cheese with a hand mixer on medium about 2 min, until completely smooth with no lumps. Any lumps now stay in the finished pie.
On low speed, beat in the condensed milk until smooth, scraping the bowl. Add the lemon juice and zest and beat 1 min. The lemon juice thickens the mixture as you beat.
Pour the filling into the cooled crust and smooth the top. Cover loosely and refrigerate at least 4 hr, or overnight, until firm enough to slice cleanly.
Top with a lemon round in the center, or one on each slice. Cut with a knife dipped in hot water and wiped dry.
tips: A store-bought 9-inch graham cracker crust works. Skip the crust steps and start with the filling.
Use fresh lemons, not bottled juice. Bottled juice tastes flat and the pie may not set as firmly.
Make it the day before. It slices more cleanly after chilling overnight.
storage: Fridge, covered, up to 4 days. Don't leave it out more than 2 hr. Freeze up to 1 month wrapped tightly and thaw in the fridge about 4 hr. Serve cold.
